increment: CI: give the python job a real PostgreSQL, run migrations, and make the integration suite actually execute
evaluator: fresh independent reviewer; this is CI plumbing, not a ledger feature, so no passes flag is in play
approval_notes: The .github/workflows/ci.yml job `python` ran `pytest -q` with no database: no services block, no DATABASE_URL, no migration step. Every integration test is guarded by pytest.mark.skipif(not DATABASE_URL), so the entire ingest, reconcile, read-API and provider layer skipped and the job still reported success.
This is not a test defect and not a product-behaviour change. tests/**, apps/** and scripts/** are zero diff. The only executable change is the workflow.

The failure mode this slice targets is a green tick that certifies nothing. Colour is therefore NOT acceptance evidence: a mis-scoped DATABASE_URL, a wrong variable name, or an unhealthy service all leave the job green and still skipping. Acceptance is by pytest count and by skip name, read from the CI log.
objective: The CI `python` job stands up PostgreSQL, applies migrations, and executes the full test suite including the integration layer, so a regression in ingest, reconcile or the read API can fail CI.
scope: .github/workflows/ci.yml, job `python` only: a postgres:16-alpine service container with a pg_isready health check; a job-scoped DATABASE_URL using the project's existing postgresql+psycopg scheme; a named `Apply database migrations` step running `alembic upgrade head` before pytest.
out_of_scope: tests/**: zero diff. No test weakened, no assertion changed, no skip marker added or removed, no xfail, no --maxfail, no continue-on-error, no `|| true`.
apps/api/app/classify/**: a confirmed fail-open on unrecognised offer_type is separately filed and is not touched.
scripts/check.ps1: its twin vacuous `npm audit --omit=dev` is separately filed and is not touched.
The ci.yml `concurrency:` block: the group does not unify push and PR refs; separately filed and not touched.
The other three CI jobs (node, secrets, dependencies): zero diff.
Any dependency pin, docker-compose.yml, migrations/**, agent-state/feature_list.json, agent-state/evaluation.json: zero diff.
Fixing any pre-existing integration failure that turning the suite on reveals. If one appears it is reported by name and stopped on, not silenced.
acceptance_criteria: A1. The CI `python` job runs a PostgreSQL service container of the SAME major version as docker-compose.yml (postgres:16-alpine), with a health check, and applies alembic migrations in a named step before pytest.
A2. DECISIVE, by count not by colour: the CI log's pytest summary line reads `1156 passed, 2 skipped` (the local base-commit measurement with a database), not the `164 skipped` of the current job.

A3. DECISIVE, by name: the only two SKIPPED lines in the CI log are tests/integration/test_stack_health.py:25 and :32, which need ATLAS_STACK_BASE_URL (a running full stack, not a database) and must stay skipped. Zero DATABASE_URL-reasoned skips.
A4. The job result is read from the step list by step name and conclusion, not from the summary tick. Every step is enumerated with its conclusion.

A5. The job is proved capable of going RED: a deliberately failing integration test is planted, CI fails at the step named `Pytest` while every earlier step still succeeds, and the revert is verified by git blob hash (git hash-object vs git rev-parse HEAD:path) rather than by git diff, since .gitattributes filters can make a diff read clean while bytes differ.
A6. No weakening anywhere in the diff: a grep for continue-on-error, `|| true`, --maxfail, xfail and skip over the changed workflow returns nothing.
A7. agent-state/progress.md is an exact append-only prefix extension of origin/main's copy, verified by comparing the first N lines byte-for-byte.
A8. The job's wall time is reported honestly against the ~9s baseline.
verification_plan: Local baseline on the base commit: an isolated postgres:16-alpine container, `alembic upgrade head`, then `pytest -q`; record the verbatim summary line and the skip list. This establishes the target numbers independently of CI.
Local guard replay: detect-secrets-hook over every tracked file against .secrets.baseline, and scripts/check_urls.py, so the new credential-shaped DATABASE_URL does not break the `secrets` job.
YAML parse of the changed workflow, printing the resolved service image, health options, job-scoped env and the ordered step names.
CI acceptance run on the draft PR: quote the pytest summary line and both SKIPPED lines verbatim from the downloaded log; enumerate the step list with conclusions via the Actions API.
CI red-proof round trip: plant, observe failure by step name, revert, verify by blob hash, observe green again.
Guardrail proof: git diff --numstat against the base commit for every guarded path.
risks: Scope of DATABASE_URL is the whole defect in miniature. Set on the pytest step alone, the migration step would fall back to migrations/env.py's default host `postgres`, which does not resolve on a runner. Job scope is deliberate and is verified by the migration step succeeding.

A service container without a health check races the suite: pytest can connect before Postgres is accepting connections, and the resulting failure looks like a test defect. Mitigated by pg_isready with the same user and database as docker-compose.yml.

The DATABASE_URL literal is credential-shaped and could trip the `secrets` job's detect-secrets baseline. Mitigated with the same `# pragma: allowlist secret` marker docker-compose.yml already uses, and verified by running the hook locally over all tracked files.
Turning 162 never-executed tests on may reveal pre-existing failures. That is a finding, not a defect of this slice; it is reported by name and not fixed here.
Wall time rises from ~9s to the order of a minute or more. Accepted: a 9s job that tests nothing is not a saving.
The red-proof commits a deliberately failing test to the PR branch for one run. It is reverted in the next commit and the revert is proved by blob hash, so final HEAD is byte-identical to pre-plant.
required_evaluation_level: Level 1 - CI infrastructure. No product code, no schema change, no Z0 logic, no security boundary. Level 2 is not triggered.
contract_review: Written after reproducing the baseline numbers locally on the base commit and BEFORE the workflow was changed, per the coding-agent instructions. Every measured claim in the handoff entry is marked as measured and separated from inference.
